meta.mission: Systematically scan every tradeline, collection, public record, and inquiry for all encoded FCRA, FDCPA, and Metro 2 violations.
meta.guarantee: For every enabled rule in this catalog, analyzeWithRulesEngine MUST evaluate it against the entire CreditReport. No rule is skipped and no triggered violation is silently dropped.

rules.description: Same tradeline has materially different delinquency/foreclosure status across bureaus (e.g., 120D late vs 180D late vs foreclosure).
rules.letterParagraph: For this account, the reported status/delinquency level differs materially between my Experian, Equifax, and TransUnion reports. The same loan cannot simultaneously show different severity levels across bureaus. This inconsistency makes the reporting misleading and fails to meet the FCRA's 'maximum possible accuracy' standard.

rules.description: Same tradeline has materially different balances/past-due amounts across bureaus (more than $50 difference).
rules.letterParagraph: The reported balance and past-due amounts for this account are inconsistent across the three credit bureaus. The same debt cannot simultaneously show different balances. This inconsistency violates FCRA's accuracy standard and must be corrected.

rules.description: Charged-off accounts should not show full balance also as 'past due'. After charge-off, Past Due field should be zero per Metro 2 guidance.
lawReferences: Metro 2 Consumer Credit Reporting Resource Guide – Charge-off coding
rules.letterParagraph: This account is reported as a charge-off but still shows the full balance as 'past due'. Under Metro 2 guidance, charged-off accounts are no longer in a repayment status and should not report past-due amounts. This non-compliant reporting is misleading.

rules.description: A third-party collector is coded as an open trade account with lates instead of a collection account.
rules.letterParagraph: This debt collector tradeline is coded as an open account with late payments instead of being reported solely as a collection account. That misclassification is misleading and inconsistent with standard Metro 2 reporting guidelines for third-party collections.

rules.description: Same collection debt is reported twice on the same bureau. Detection uses four paths: (1) bureauAccountId match, (2) account number match (4+ digits), (3) DOFD match, or (4) openedDate match with both names matching. All paths require exact balance match.
rules.letterParagraph: The same collection debt appears multiple times on my credit report, which unfairly doubles the negative impact of a single alleged debt. Reporting the same debt multiple times is misleading and does not satisfy the FCRA requirement that consumer reports be prepared with maximum possible accuracy.

rules.description: Original creditor shows $0 balance and 'sold' remark but still coded as active charge-off/collection status.
rules.letterParagraph: This original creditor account shows a $0 balance with 'sold' or 'transferred' remarks but still reports a charge-off or collection status. Under Metro 2 standards, a sold account with zero balance should not maintain an active derogatory status. This is misleading and inaccurate.

rules.description: Same tradeline reports materially different balance or past-due amounts across bureaus for the same debt.
Tradeline status severity differs between bureaus (e.g., foreclosure vs 120 days late) for the same underlying mortgage or loan.
Date of First Delinquency (DOFD) appears to have been moved later to make a derogatory item look newer (re-aging).
Negative account or collection is still reporting more than 7 years after DOFD.
Account previously disputed by consumer but is not marked as disputed on one or more bureaus.
Multiple tradelines appear to represent the same debt, inflating derogatory impact.
Collection account does not clearly list the original creditor when expected.
Charged-off tradeline still shows full balance as past-due, contrary to Metro 2 charge-off guidance.
lawReferences: Metro 2 Consumer Credit Reporting Resource Guide – Charge-off coding

rules.description: Third-party collection is coded as an open revolving/installment account with late history instead of a collection.
Account sold to another lender still carries an active charge-off/collection status instead of pure sold/transferred coding.
Collector continues reporting a disputed debt without proper validation.
